examples.input:
Competition: Net Zero Aviation Fuels

Funding available: Share of up to £12 million
Project size: £2 million to £5 million
Competition opens: 15 January 2025
Competition closes: 12 March 2025 11:00am

Scope:
We are looking for innovative projects that can accelerate the development and scale-up of sustainable aviation fuels (SAF). Projects should address one or more of:
- Novel SAF production pathways
- Feedstock development and supply chain
- Integration with airport infrastructure
- Certification and testing methodologies

Your project must:
- Be collaborative, involving at least two organisations
- Include an end user (airline, airport, or fuel supplier)
- Demonstrate a clear route to commercialisation
- Address TRL 4-7 technologies

Eligibility:
- UK registered businesses
- Must include at least one SME
- Academic partners welcome but industry-led

output.title: Net Zero Aviation Fuels
output.summary: Innovate UK competition seeking innovative projects to accelerate sustainable aviation fuel development and scale-up, with £12m funding available for collaborative projects at TRL 4-7.
output.problemStatement: Aviation lacks scalable, cost-effective alternatives to kerosene-based jet fuel, blocking the sector's path to net zero emissions.

examples.input:
Clean Maritime Plan 2025 Update

The Department for Transport has published an update to the Clean Maritime Plan, setting out the government's strategy for decarbonising the maritime sector.

Key commitments:
- All new vessels operating in UK waters to be zero-emission capable by 2035
- £200 million Green Shipping Corridor Fund to establish zero-emission routes
- Requirement for major ports to provide shore power by 2030
- Support for domestic hydrogen and ammonia bunkering infrastructure

The plan identifies priority corridors:
- UK-Rotterdam for freight
- Belfast-Liverpool for passenger ferries
- Scottish island routes for community resilience

Industry will be expected to:
- Submit decarbonisation plans by 2026
- Report emissions annually
- Participate in voluntary efficiency schemes

The Maritime and Coastguard Agency will develop new regulatory frameworks for alternative fuels.

output.title: Clean Maritime Plan 2025 Update
output.summary: DfT strategy update mandating zero-emission capable vessels by 2035, establishing £200m Green Shipping Corridor Fund, and requiring port shore power by 2030.
output.problemStatement: UK maritime sector lacks clear regulatory pathway and infrastructure for transition to zero-emission operations.

modes.reasoning: Explicitly maritime: vessels, ports, shipping corridors

examples.input:
HORIZON-CL5-2025-D5-01: Next Generation Rail Systems

Type of Action: Research and Innovation Action (RIA)
Budget: €15,000,000
Deadline: 18 September 2025

Expected Outcome:
Projects should contribute to the European Rail Research Advisory Council (ERRAC) vision for a sustainable, efficient rail system by 2050.

Scope:
Proposals should address the development of:
- Digital automatic coupling (DAC) for freight wagons
- AI-based predictive maintenance systems
- Energy-efficient traction systems
- Cross-border interoperability solutions

TRL: Projects should start at TRL 3-4 and reach TRL 5-6.

Consortium requirements:
- Minimum 3 independent legal entities from 3 different EU/associated countries
- Must include at least one infrastructure manager or railway undertaking
- UK entities eligible as associated country participants

output.title: Next Generation Rail Systems (HORIZON-CL5-2025-D5-01)
output.summary: Horizon Europe RIA funding €15m for rail innovation projects covering digital coupling, AI maintenance, energy efficiency, and cross-border interoperability at TRL 3-6.
output.problemStatement: European rail lacks standardised digital systems for freight, predictive maintenance capabilities, and seamless cross-border operations.
eligibility: Infrastructure manager or railway undertaking required

modes.reasoning: Explicitly rail: wagons, traction, railway undertakings

challengeType.reasoning: TRL advancement, R&I action, technology development

examples.input:
SBRI Competition: Smart Motorway Safety Enhancement

National Highways is seeking innovative solutions to improve safety on smart motorways.

Phase 1: Feasibility studies up to £100,000 (6 months)
Phase 2: Development contracts up to £1,000,000 (12 months)

Challenge areas:
1. Stopped vehicle detection - improving detection speed and accuracy
2. Emergency refuge area signage - enhanced visibility in all conditions
3. Driver information systems - real-time hazard communication
4. Hard shoulder running management - safer dynamic lane control

We welcome solutions using:
- Computer vision and AI
- V2X communication
- IoT sensors
- Advanced materials for signage

Submission deadline: 28 February 2025

Open to UK registered businesses. SMEs particularly encouraged.

output.title: Smart Motorway Safety Enhancement
output.summary: SBRI competition from National Highways seeking safety innovations for smart motorways, with Phase 1 feasibility (£100k) and Phase 2 development (£1m) contracts available.
output.problemStatement: Smart motorways have safety concerns around stopped vehicle detection, emergency refuge visibility, and dynamic lane management that require technological solutions.

modes.reasoning: Smart motorways, hard shoulder, National Highways

themes.reasoning: AI, computer vision, V2X, IoT sensors

examples.input:
Hydrogen Transport Innovation Programme

UKRI Opportunity
Funding: £30 million total, projects £1m-£5m
Closing date: 5 May 2025

This cross-modal programme supports the development of hydrogen technologies across transport modes.

Scope includes:
- Heavy goods vehicle hydrogen powertrains
- Hydrogen refuelling infrastructure for multiple transport modes
- Maritime vessel hydrogen propulsion systems
- Rail hydrogen traction technology
- Aviation ground support equipment using hydrogen

Projects must demonstrate:
- Application across 2+ transport modes
- Clear pathway to reducing infrastructure costs
- Collaboration with end users in relevant sectors
- TRL 4-7

We particularly welcome projects addressing:
- Shared refuelling infrastructure (e.g., combined road and rail depots)
- Standardisation of hydrogen storage and handling
- Safety certification across modes

output.title: Hydrogen Transport Innovation Programme
output.summary: UKRI £30m cross-modal programme supporting hydrogen technology development across HGVs, maritime, rail, and aviation ground operations, requiring multi-modal applications at TRL 4-7.
output.problemStatement: Hydrogen transport deployment is hindered by siloed development across modes, leading to duplicated infrastructure costs and lack of standardisation.

modes.reasoning: Explicitly requires 2+ modes, addresses shared infrastructure

examples.input:
Transport Skills and Workforce Development Fund

The Department for Transport is launching a new fund to address critical skills gaps in the transport sector.

Funding: £15 million over 3 years
Project size: £100,000 to £500,000

Priority areas:
- Digital skills for transport operations (data analytics, AI/ML basics)
- Green skills for vehicle maintenance (EV, hydrogen systems)
- Diversity and inclusion in transport careers
- Apprenticeship development for emerging transport technologies

Eligible applicants:
- Further education colleges
- Universities with transport-related courses
- Industry training providers
- Transport operators with training programmes

Deadline: Rolling applications until fund exhausted

Projects should demonstrate clear industry demand and pathway to employment.

output.title: Transport Skills and Workforce Development Fund
output.summary: DfT £15m fund addressing transport sector skills gaps in digital, green technology maintenance, diversity, and emerging tech apprenticeships.
output.problemStatement: Transport sector faces critical skills shortages in digital operations, green vehicle maintenance, and lacks diversity, threatening ability to deliver net zero transition.

examples.input:
Mobility as a Service (MaaS) Integration Challenge

Innovate UK in partnership with Transport for the North

Funding: £8 million
Project size: Up to £2 million

Challenge:
Develop and demonstrate integrated mobility platforms that seamlessly connect public transport, shared mobility, and active travel options.

We're looking for:
- Single ticketing solutions across multiple operators
- Real-time journey planning with live disruption handling
- Integration of bike-share, e-scooters, car clubs with public transport
- Accessibility features for users with mobility requirements
- Data sharing frameworks between transport providers

Demonstrator locations:
- Manchester city region
- Leeds city region
- Sheffield city region

Must involve:
- At least one local transport authority
- At least one technology provider
- Public transport operators

Deadline: 1 April 2025

output.title: Mobility as a Service (MaaS) Integration Challenge
output.summary: Innovate UK £8m challenge with Transport for the North to develop integrated mobility platforms connecting public transport, shared mobility, and active travel with single ticketing.
output.problemStatement: Fragmented transport options with separate ticketing, planning, and payment systems create barriers to seamless multi-modal journeys and sustainable transport choices.

modes.reasoning: Explicitly multi-modal integration, MaaS, ticketing across modes

examples.input:
Digital Railway Data Platform Innovation

Network Rail Open Call for Innovation

We are seeking innovative approaches to creating a unified data platform for railway operations.

Challenge:
Railway data exists in silos across multiple systems. We need solutions that can:
- Integrate data from legacy signalling systems
- Provide real-time asset condition monitoring
- Enable predictive analytics for maintenance scheduling
- Support digital twin development for infrastructure planning
- Ensure cybersecurity across connected systems

We're particularly interested in:
- API development for legacy system integration
- Edge computing for trackside data processing
- Secure data sharing with train operating companies

Funding: Up to £500,000 per project
Timeline: 18 month projects

Open to UK businesses with relevant data/digital expertise.

output.title: Digital Railway Data Platform Innovation
output.summary: Network Rail innovation call seeking solutions for unified railway data platform integrating legacy systems, enabling real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and digital twins.
output.problemStatement: Railway operational data is siloed across disconnected legacy systems, preventing effective real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and digital transformation.

modes.reasoning: Network Rail, railway operations, signalling, trackside

challengeType.reasoning: Data platform, API, digital twin - explicitly digital focus
